statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-12345 is a race in the cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, reported upstream at https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 and fixed upstream only on the 3.12 and later branches, by https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157580 and its backports. The CVE record at https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345 lists CPython before 3.12.15 as affected. No backport to the 3.10 branch has been proposed upstream, so no CPython 3.10 release carries the fix. No published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.10 package carries a backport. In every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8), /usr/lib/python3.10/tempfile.py and shutil.py in the python-3.10 package are identical to Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py in the matching upstream 3.10 release, and the compiled tempfile and shutil modules in the python-3.10-pycache-pyc0, -pyc1 and -pyc2 packages contain none of the names the proposed 3.11 backport adds (_rmtree_use_dir_fd, _resetperms_at, _resetperms_fd, parent_fd, orig_entry). Every published build is affected. No upstream fix exists for the 3.10 branch; the fix is pending an upstream 3.10 backport, or a DHI backport of the upstream change.

CVE-2026-12345: the cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory raced with changes to the tree, so an attacker who swaps a directory for a symbolic link during cleanup could get files outside the temporary directory deleted. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/c39b52d00b42200aaadff679e2fe3f1006d57c58), first released in CPython 3.12.16. The CVE record (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345) names 3.12.15 as fixed, but an earlier backport was reverted before that release (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e1f3590f155c6d66007e958c98c9d69316551993) and the v3.12.15 tempfile.py and shutil.py do not have the fix. Checked Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py for the fd-relative cleanup the fix adds (_onexc_kwargs) in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.16-r0 lack the fix; 3.12.16-r0 and every later build have it. The range ends at 3.12.16-r0.

The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory raced with changes to the tree: an attacker able to modify the directory during cleanup could replace a subdirectory with a symbolic link, so files outside the temporary directory were deleted or had their permissions reset with the privileges of the cleaning process. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/0478b52788117db4b831b3efd648f56b777628aa), first released in CPython 3.13.18; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345. The CVE record notes that the fix does not cover platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false; on Linux shutil.rmtree uses the file-descriptor based implementation, for which it is true. The record also says file flags may still be reset outside the tree on all platforms; that path goes through os.chflags, which Python does not provide on Linux (Linux has no chflags system call), so the shipped TemporaryDirectory cleanup skips resetting file flags there. Compared Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py in the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4) with the upstream CPython releases; both architectures agree, and each build ships the upstream files for its CPython version (the version string in libpython3.13.so). 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.17-r0 are built from CPython 3.13.17 or earlier and lack the fixed TemporaryDirectory cleanup; 3.13.18-r0, the first build of CPython 3.13.18, and every later build have it. The range ends at 3.13.18-r0.

CVE-2026-12345: the cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory races with changes to the directory tree. An attacker who can modify the tree during cleanup can replace a subdirectory with a symbolic link, so files outside the temporary directory are deleted or have their permissions and file flags reset, with the privileges of the process doing the cleanup: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345 and https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 . The fix for the 3.15 branch is commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/06ef3d43fdaf4da97af12fa694b4886092c4b970 , the backport of https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157580 ; outside tests, documentation and its NEWS entry it changes Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py. It is in CPython 3.15.0rc3, 3.15.0 and 3.15.2, and the CVE record lists 3.15.0rc3 as the first fixed 3.15 release. The record adds that platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false remain affected, and that file flags may still be reset outside the tree on all platforms. A later main-branch change for the same issue, https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/aa17c688d2c160969f2c8963f4454cdd139808e7 , fixes the cleanup fallbacks for temporary directories created with bytes paths; upstream filed it as a Library change, not a Security one, and it is not in any 3.15 release up to 3.15.2. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes six python-3.15 builds, 3.15.0-r0, 3.15.2-r0, 3.15.2-r1, 3.15.2-r2, 3.15.2-r3 and 3.15.2-r4, for x86_64 and aarch64. We downloaded the python-3.15, python-3.15-pycache-pyc0, python-3.15-pycache-pyc1 and python-3.15-pycache-pyc2 packages of every build on both architectures, and the pyc-3.15 and python-3.15-pyc packages, which hold no files; each was verified against its index checksum. In every build, /usr/lib/python3.15/tempfile.py and /usr/lib/python3.15/shutil.py are byte-identical to Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py in the upstream CPython 3.15.0 and 3.15.2 releases, which are the same in both, so every build has the fixed cleanup. The compiled tempfile and shutil modules in the three pycache packages are checked-hash .pyc files whose source hash matches those files. Running each build's own python3.15 (3.15.0 in 3.15.0-r0, 3.15.2 in the later builds) shows that shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is True and that the os module has no chflags or lchflags function, so the cleanup's file-flag reset in tempfile does nothing on these builds. 3.15.0-r0, the lowest published build, carries the fix, so the range ends there.

CVE-2026-12345: the cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory raced with changes to the tree, so an attacker who swaps a directory for a symbolic link during cleanup could get files outside the temporary directory deleted. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/c39b52d00b42200aaadff679e2fe3f1006d57c58), first released in CPython 3.12.16. The CVE record (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345) names 3.12.15 as fixed, but an earlier backport was reverted before that release (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e1f3590f155c6d66007e958c98c9d69316551993) and the v3.12.15 tempfile.py and shutil.py do not have the fix. Checked Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py for the fd-relative cleanup the fix adds (_onexc_kwargs) in the standard library shipped by these packages (libpython-3.12-stdlib and libpython-3.12-minimal) in every build published in the DHI Debian repository, 3.12.13-0 to 3.12.16-8, amd64 and arm64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.16-0 lack the fix; 3.12.16-0 and every later build have it. The range ends at 3.12.16-0.

The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory raced with changes to the tree: an attacker able to modify the directory during cleanup could replace a subdirectory with a symbolic link, so files outside the temporary directory were deleted or had their permissions reset with the privileges of the cleaning process. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157579 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/0478b52788117db4b831b3efd648f56b777628aa), first released in CPython 3.13.18; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345. The CVE record notes that the fix does not cover platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false; on Linux shutil.rmtree uses the file-descriptor based implementation, for which it is true. The record also says file flags may still be reset outside the tree on all platforms; that path goes through os.chflags, which Python does not provide on Linux (Linux has no chflags system call), so the shipped TemporaryDirectory cleanup skips resetting file flags there. Compared Lib/tempfile.py and Lib/shutil.py in the standard library shipped by the DHI Debian 13 libpython-3.13-stdlib and libpython-3.13-minimal packages in every published build on amd64 and arm64 (3.13.13-0 to 3.13.18-7) with the upstream CPython releases; both architectures agree, and each build ships the upstream files for its CPython version (the version string in libpython3.13.so). 3.13.13-0 to 3.13.17-0 are built from CPython 3.13.17 or earlier and lack the fixed TemporaryDirectory cleanup; 3.13.18-0, the first build of CPython 3.13.18, and every later build have it. The range ends at 3.13.18-0.
